page.title: Cáirde Corrin - caring for land, connecting community
page.description: A community group protecting, restoring and celebrating the Glenabo-Corrin catchment above Fermoy, Co. Cork.

subject.name: Glenabo catchment
subject.description: The Glenabo catchment covers about 3.6 km² (about 360 ha) and falls from 213 m to its outlet at about 21 m OD on the Munster Blackwater (HA 18). Longest flow path about 4 km.

hero.title: Glenabo
hero.intro: An historical land where all living things can thrive in harmony with nature.
hero.line2: Everything that falls here ends up in the Blackwater.
hero.line3: About 360 hectares. One outlet. A catchment small enough that a community can change what comes down it.

blocks.eyebrow: The ground we are talking about
blocks.heading:
Everything that falls here
ends up in the Blackwater.
blocks.text: A catchment is not an opinion. It is the exact area of ground whose surface water drains to one point. Ours drains to a single confluence on the *Munster Blackwater* at the northern tip of Glenabo Wood, and it can be drawn.

blocks.alt: Map of the Glenabo hydrological catchment showing boundary, modelled channel network and outlet to the Munster Blackwater
blocks.caption: The Glenabo hydrological catchment, its modelled channel network, and the outlet to the Munster Blackwater.

blocks.heading:
Same hill.
Same morning.
blocks.text: One hundred and thirty-six metres apart on the same slope. What separates them is what was planted here, and when.

items.alt: Widely spaced slim broadleaf trunks with a thick green grass and herb layer covering the ground
items.caption: Broadleaf, widely spaced. Light reaches the floor and the ground is green.

items.alt: Closely spaced straight conifer trunks above a floor of bare brown needle litter, ivy at the lower edge
items.caption: Even-aged conifer, planted close. The floor is bare needle litter.

blocks.heading: One point on the *Blackwater*.
blocks.text:
About three hundred and sixty hectares drain through a single confluence. Upstream of it, every field, track, drain and stand of trees is part of the same system. Downstream, it is somebody else's water.

That is why we work to a catchment rather than a parish.

blocks.heading:
Catchment, woodland and amenity
inside one working boundary.
blocks.text: The hydrological catchment is the scientific unit. The area we propose to work in is larger, because Corrin Hill, Corrin Wood and Knockananig Reservoir belong to the same landscape and the same walk, even where they drain elsewhere.

blocks.alt: Map of the proposed area for action around Glenabo, Corrin Hill and Knockananig Reservoir
blocks.caption: The proposed area for action, taking in the Glenabo catchment, Glenabo Wood, Corrin Hill and Knockananig Reservoir.

blocks.heading: The three strands of our work are
blocks.text: We work to protect, restore and celebrate the environment, heritage and recreational use of our Glenabo-Corrin waterways, engaging with our local community, partnering with agencies, and taking action to ensure the rivers and their valleys flourish for future generations.

items.label: Strand 1
items.heading: Points of interest
items.text: Enhancing existing trails to include information on the ecology, history and folklore of our area

items.label: Strand 2
items.heading: New spaces
items.text: Developing new local recreational and educational amenities in the Glenabo/Corrin catchment

items.label: Strand 3
items.heading: Improving water and ecosystems
items.text: Working with other local and national community, state, voluntary, educational and outdoor activity bodies to improve the water quality and biodiversity of our target area

blocks.heading:
It is a small catchment.
That is the good news.
blocks.text: About three hundred and sixty hectares is walkable in a morning and knowable in a season. Survey work, invasive species removal, recording what is here - none of it needs a specialist to start.
